tool_summary: JavaScript/TypeScript runtime and package manager. Handles both dependency installation (bun install, bun add) and script/file execution (bun run, bun <file>) in one binary.
platform_notes: bun behavior is consistent across Linux and macOS.

rules.description: The run subcommand, or invoking bun directly with a file path, executes JavaScript/TypeScript code. The file's content is not inspected by commandant.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on the script's contents, which commandant does not inspect.

rules.description: The --registry flag points bun at a package registry other than the default. Installing from an untrusted or unfamiliar registry is a common supply-chain attack vector, since installed packages' lifecycle scripts run with the invoking user's privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but its lifecycle scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The add/install subcommands install packages, which by default run lifecycle scripts (postinstall, etc.) with the invoking user's privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but lifecycle scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Manages packages or runs JavaScript/TypeScript code. Read-only subcommands (pm ls) do not alter system state. Severity here reflects that unrecognized or future bun subcommands fall through to this rule; known read-only subcommands are not themselves being flagged as risky.
rules.notes: Default bumped to WARNING (not INFO) because this tool's CLI surface evolves quickly; an unmatched/unrecognized subcommand should surface for review rather than silently pass as benign.
